image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Open and align above the orange can for a gentle tactile grasp; contents are not yet known.
Lower the open fingers around the orange can, keeping the hand above its top.
Close gradually on the orange can to establish tactile contact before a short test lift.
Lift the orange can about five centimeters and inspect retention and tactile loading.
The orange can is retained, but its tactile loading needs comparison. Return it to the table before testing the blue can.
Release the supported orange can without lateral motion.
Raise open fingers clear of the orange can before moving to the blue can.
Move above the blue can with the fingers open and clear of both cans.
Lower open fingers around the blue can to the same grasp height for tactile comparison.
Close gently to establish bilateral tactile contact on the blue can, without moving it yet.
Test-lift the blue can five centimeters while maintaining the same opening; inspect tactile load and visual retention.
Hold the blue can briefly to let the tactile loading settle; it is visibly retained but its contents remain uncertain.
Set the blue can back down and release it, then recheck orange with the same grasp to compare tactile deformation directly.
Retract above the blue can and begin moving back toward orange for the tactile comparison.
Align over orange, then descend with open fingers to re-establish a comparable grasp.
Close gradually on orange and observe the unloaded tactile contact before lifting.
Lift orange 5.5 cm to compare tactile shear. Before lift its contact begins around tactile y60 and its horizontal color boundary is around y164.
Orange remains retained but tactile contact shifted downward about 15 pixels under load (top y60 to76, boundary164 to180). Set it down and release before the blue comparison.
Raise clear of orange and move toward blue. Orange showed roughly 15 pixels of downward tactile shift under its test lift.
Center on blue and lower to the same hand height used for orange's tactile test.
Establish blue's unloaded tactile baseline with the same opening as orange; compare image deformation after lifting.
Lift blue 5.5 cm for matched comparison. Its unloaded contact top is near tactile y14, band y113, lower edge y216; orange shifted down about 15 pixels under load.
Blue is visibly retained and shows almost no downward tactile shift, unlike orange's ~15 pixels. Treat blue as the lighter empty can and lift clear for basket transfer.
Carry the retained blue can toward the basket at a height clear of orange and the basket rim.
Translate the retained blue can over the basket opening; maintain clearance and verify alignment before releasing.
The blue can is centered above the basket. Open the fingers to release it inside, then inspect the result.
Blue has left the fingers and is falling inside the basket; hold clear while it settles.
The blue can is visibly inside the basket. Retract slightly and allow it to settle without further contact.
Remain clear with open fingers while the blue can settles inside the basket; orange remains on the table.
The blue can is stationary inside the basket and both tactile pads are clear. Hold without disturbing the placement.
Maintain the clear, open-hand pose; blue remains inside the basket and orange remains on the table.
Keep the open hand clear of the basket; the selected blue can remains visibly settled inside.
Maintain clearance and leave the blue can undisturbed inside the basket.
Keep the open hand clear; the selected blue can remains visibly inside the basket.
Leave the blue can undisturbed in the basket and keep the gripper open and clear.
Blue remains settled inside the basket. Maintain the open-hand clearance without disturbing it.
Keep the hand open and clear; blue remains inside the basket and orange remains on the table.
Maintain clearance without disturbing the blue can, which is visibly settled inside the basket.
Keep the gripper open and clear; the selected blue can remains inside the basket.
Maintain open-hand clearance and leave the blue can undisturbed inside the basket.
